title: A colourful tower
description: Start with 28 blocks, then make it your own.
prompt: Create a tower with seven layers of four cubes. Use cyan, pink and yellow. Frame the whole tower and slowly orbit around it.

title: A burst of colour
description: Launch, freeze the action, orbit and let it tumble.
prompt: Create a colourful block explosion with a dramatic cinematic style.

title: Words in orbit
description: A real 3D ring of letters around a simple shape.
prompt: Create a cyan sphere and a golden 3D ring reading CREATE / VIEW / SHARE around it. Anchor the ring in world space, rotate it slowly and orbit the camera.

title: Your first three shapes
description: Create, recolour and resize three simple objects.
prompt: Create a cyan cube, a pink sphere and a golden cone side by side. Let them appear with blue edges and slowly orbit the camera.
steps: Create three objects and compare their silhouettes.
Ask: Make the sphere larger and change the cube to purple.
Use Save scene to download a .scene file. Reopen it later to keep editing.

title: Let gravity do the work
description: Watch blocks and balls fall, bounce and settle.
prompt: Create a small stack of colourful blocks and balls above the ground. Let them fall with realistic collisions and subtle impact sounds.
steps: Create the objects with dynamic physics.
Start the simulation and listen to the impacts.
Pause to inspect a collision, then resume. Reset returns to the starting poses.

title: A closer look
description: Move from a close detail to a smooth wider orbit.
prompt: Create a small colourful sculpture. Start the camera close, slowly pull back to reveal it and blend into a gentle orbit.
steps: Frame the subject close without cutting it off.
Pull back, then blend smoothly into the orbit.
Ask: Show it from the other side, keeping the motion smooth.

title: A command comes to life
description: Animated typing, quiet cues and a glowing confirmation.
prompt: Show an animated command field typing “Make it blue”, then validate it softly and turn the sculpture blue. Use command-input-v2.
steps: The command field is an illustrative film overlay; it does not contact an AI.
Typing and validation sounds come from command-input-v2.
The scene change is authored in the same timeline, after validation.
control_note: This snippet adds the illustrative command field only. The blue colour change is a separate action in the downloadable scene.

title: Make the ending yours
description: Keep the Polynite signature, choose its placement and soften its sound.
prompt: Use polynite-ending-v4 for this film. Put the closing signature higher with the short-portrait layout and lower its sound volume to 0.5.
steps: Exports install the required signature automatically; creation prompts do not need to mention it.
For a custom ending, stop the film and install polynite-ending-v4.
Choose default or short-portrait placement and adjust volume. The fade, shine-only bloom and quiet cues stay together.
The signature remains required at export; paid removal is not enabled.

title: From scene to MP4
description: Record a smooth film, preview it and keep your own copy.
prompt: Record this scene from the beginning as a landscape MP4 at 1080p and 60 FPS. Keep the sounds subtle, then show me where to download the video.
steps: Prepare a film with the scene and camera moves. Save a .scene copy if you want to edit it later.
Record from the beginning; do not pre-play the film. Choose landscape or portrait and 30 or 60 FPS.
After recording, open Gallery > Videos. Preview with sound, then download the MP4 or use Open folder on desktop.
A .scene stays editable. An MP4 is the rendered movie. A Mint Link opens the interactive creation.
Download cloud videos you want to keep: uploaded MCP videos have seven-day retention.

title: A forest under colourful rain
description: Static tree colliders meet falling spheres and cubes.
prompt: Create a small stylised forest with solid trunks and canopies. Drop colourful spheres and cubes onto it, with collisions, subtle sounds and a slow camera orbit.
steps: Keep the tree trunks and canopies static, with colliders.
Use dynamic bodies only for the falling shapes.
Test a small rain first, then increase the count.
Frame the whole forest so the collisions remain easy to follow.

title: One push, a chain reaction
description: A small impulse sends a row of coloured dominos tumbling.
prompt: Create a row of colourful dominos. Give the first one a gentle push and let the chain reaction unfold. Keep the camera close enough to see every collision.
steps: Use thin upright blocks and leave enough space for one to touch the next as it falls.
Give only the first block an initial tilt and angular velocity.
Use Reset scene to replay from the authored poses.
Change the spacing or friction and compare how far the chain travels.
